answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying influence to a refundable bond plus attested work history. A new identity starts with zero trust and must complete real, peer-verified jobs before it can vote or claim payouts; cheating slashes its bond. Like a grove that takes seasons to mature, trust cannot be bought overnight, and a velvet-smooth flood of fresh fakes still faces the same slow voyage: each clone must separately stake funds and build a job record, so forging a thousand voters costs a thousand bonds and histories, breaking the attacker's economics.
